  def fix_provides(provides)
    name_re = /^[^ \(]+/

    if !name.nil?
      remainder = provides[name.length..-1].to_s
      trimmed = remainder.lstrip
      if trimmed.start_with?("(")
        close_index = trimmed.rindex(")")
        inner = ""
        if !close_index.nil?
          inner = trimmed[1...close_index].to_s.strip
        end
        inner_match = inner.match(/^([<>=]+)\s+(.+)$/)
        if inner_match
          relation = inner_match[1]
          version_text = inner_match[2]
        else
          op_only = inner.match(/^([<>=]+)$/)
          if op_only
            relation = op_only[1]
          else
            version_text = inner
          end
        end
      else
        bare_match = trimmed.match(/^([<>=~]+)\s*(.*)$/)
        if bare_match
          relation = bare_match[1]
          version_text = bare_match[2]
        end
      end

      if !relation.nil?
        mapped_relation = {:< => "<<", :> => ">>"}[relation.to_sym]
        if mapped_relation.nil?
          mapped_relation = debianize_op(relation)
        end
        if mapped_relation != relation
          logger.debug("Keeping original provides operator", :operator => relation, :debianized => mapped_relation)
        end
      end

      if !version_text.nil?
        version_re = /^(?:([0-9]+):)?(.+?)(?:-(.*))?$/
        version_match = version_re.match(version_text)
        current_version = version
        if attributes[:version_given?]
          given_version = attributes.fetch(:version)
          logger.debug("Command-line version is present while normalizing provides", :version => given_version)
        end
        if version_match
          provides_epoch = version_match[1]
          provides_upstream = version_match[2]
          provides_revision = version_match[3]
          if provides_upstream == current_version
            logger.debug("Provides upstream version matches package version",
                         :provides => provides,
                         :version => current_version,
                         :epoch => epoch,
                         :iteration => iteration,
                         :provides_epoch => provides_epoch,
                         :provides_revision => provides_revision)
          end
        end

        constraint_op = relation
        if constraint_op.nil?
          constraint_op = "="
        end
        constraint = "#{name} #{constraint_op} #{version_text}"
        expanded = expand_pessimistic_constraints(constraint)
        constraint_name, constraint_operator, constraint_ver = constraint.split(/\s+/)
        version_components = constraint_ver.to_s.split(".").collect { |v| v.to_i }

                     :constraint_operator => constraint_operator,
                     :version_components => version_components,
                     :version_prefix => version_prefix,
                     :portion => portion_to_work_with,
                     :expanded => expanded)
        if expanded.length > 1
          logger.debug("Pessimistic provides constraint is not rewritten for debian",
                       :provides => provides,
                       :expanded => expanded)
        end
      end
    end

    if name =~ /[A-Z]/
      logger.warn("Downcasing provides '#{name}' because deb packages " \
                   " don't work so good with uppercase names")
      provides = provides.gsub(name_re) { |n| n.downcase }

describe "#output with Provides values" do
    let(:original) { FPM::Package::Deb.new }

    before do
      # output a package, use it as the input, set the subject to that input
      # package. This helps ensure that we can write and read packages
      # properly.

      original.name = "name"
      original.version = "123"
    end

    after do
      original.cleanup
    end # after

    invalid = [
      "this is not valid",
      "hello = world",
      "hello ()",
      "hello (>)",
      "hello (1234)",
      "foo (<< 1.0.0-54)"
    ]

    valid = [
      "libc",
      "libc (= 6)",
      "bar (= 1:1.0)",
      "bar (= 1:1.0-1)",
      "foo (= 1.0.0-54)"
    ]

    invalid.each do |i|
      it "should reject '#{i}'" do
        original.provides << i

        insist { original.output(target) }.raises FPM::InvalidPackageConfiguration
      end
    end

    valid.each do |i|
      it "should accept '#{i}'" do
        original.provides << i

        original.output(target)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "#reproducible" do

    let(:package) {
       # Turn on reproducible build behavior by setting SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH like user would
       val = FPM::Package::Deb.new
       val.attributes[:source_date_epoch] = '1'  # one second into Jan 1 1970 UTC... '0' not supported by zlib binding :-(
       val

  # Validate a provides entry according to Debian policy:

  # A versioned relational clause is only allowed with the '=' operator,
  # and the version must be a valid Debian version string.
  # Ref: https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/ch-relationships.html
  def valid_provides?(provides)
    m = /^([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*)\s*(?:\(\s*(<<|<=|=|>=|>>)\s*([^\s()]+)\s*\))?$/.match(provides)
    return false if m.nil?

    # Versioned provides only allow the '=' operator
    return false if !m[2].nil? && m[2] != "="

    # If a version is given, it must be a valid Debian version string
    version = m[3]
    if !version.nil?
      return false unless version =~ /^(?:[0-9]+:)?[0-9][A-Za-z0-9.+:~-]*(?:-[A-Za-z0-9.~+]+)?$/
